claims.text: The gradient of a straight-line graph is found from a triangle drawn with two points on the line that are far apart, covering at least half of the line: gradient = Δy/Δx, with the unit of y divided by the unit of x.

verification.method: Authored originally for the 9702 structural exemplar under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Where the x-axis does not start at zero, the y-intercept cannot be read off the graph; it is calculated from c = y − mx using a point on the line.

claims.text: The absolute uncertainty in a repeated reading is half the range of the repeats; the percentage uncertainty is the absolute uncertainty divided by the value, × 100%.
